item.title: Aging population puts pressure on dental care
item.description:
Aging population puts pressure on dental care

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

New research by Rabobank shows that the country’s aging population will put pressure on dental care providers.

A report published on Monday warns that there are not enough dentists too keep up with the specialsed needs of the elderly.

“The increasing aging of the population also brings with it changing challenges in terms of knowledge and the way of working in dental practices,” the report says.

In 2045, more than one in seven residents of the Netherlands will be older than 75, compared to one in ten now.

The proportion of people over 75 without their own teeth has fallen considerably in the last two decades, thanks to technological advancements and the improved financial situation for many later in life. As such, older people often need more frequent and specialised care including the maintenance of crowns, bridges and implants.

On average, a person over 75 contacted the dentist 3.2 times a year in 2025, compared to 1.6 times in 2014, the report says.

The professional association KNMT warned the House of Representatives in 2021 that a shortage of service providers was loom and called for more capacity to train dentists.

Currently, there are 259 dental training places at three universities. Last year, the education ministry decided to gradually expand the number of dentistry study places to 290 by 2027.

The gaps are already being filled by dentists from other countries. Some 25 percent of the dentists working in the Netherlands were trained abroad and that number continues to rise.

item.title: ICC’s chief prosecutor dismissed over sexual misconduct claims
item.description:
ICC’s chief prosecutor dismissed over sexual misconduct claims

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The chief prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, Karim Khan, has been dismissed after a member states voted to remove him over allegations of sexual misconduct.

The 56-year-old British lawyer was relieved of his duties more than a year ago at his own request after members of his team, including a 39-year-old Malaysian lawyer, came forward with detailed claims of harassment.

Khan vigorously denied the allegations, but an internal investigation at the court, based in The Hague, concluded in June that he had committed a “serious breach of duty” by having a sexual relationship with a junior member of staff. He subsequently tried to pressure her into dropping her complaint, the inquiry found.

Supporters of Khan claimed he had been the victim of a smear campaign linked to his decision to issue arrest warrants for Israel’s prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant as part of an investigation into war crimes in Gaza.

It is the first time a prosecutor has been dismissed by the ICC in connection with a disciplinary investigation. Khan’s lawyer said he would challenge “the lawfulness and fairness of the decision”, but it is not clear what legal avenues are available.

“Brick by brick”

The vote by a two-thirds majority of the ICC’s 125 members comes at a time when the court is coming under renewed pressure from the United States government.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed the court was a threat to American sovereignty and vowed to dismantle the institution “brick by brick”.

In an op-ed in the Wall Street Journal, Rubio claimed US border officials and elected leaders could be “dragged before an international court” and tried by foreign judges for the “so-called ‘crime’ of defending their own country.”

In fact, the ICC has no jurisdiction on US soil because the United States is not a member state.

In 2002 Congress passed the American Service-Members’ Protection Act (ASPA), nicknamed the Hague Invasion Act, which authorises the president to use “all means necessary and appropriate”, including military intervention, to release any American services personnel detained or imprisoned by the ICC.

item.title: Drive to recruit more teachers sparks 13.5% rise in applications
item.description:
Drive to recruit more teachers sparks 13.5% rise in applications

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

More university students are opting for teacher training courses, raising hopes of an end to the shortage of staff in schools, latest figures show.

The number of new registrations increased by 13.5% last year, according to figures from Universiteiten van Nederland (UNL) reported by Trouw.

UNL chairman Caspar van den Berg said the development was “very good news” for efforts to tackle a nationwide shortage of 13,000 teachers in primary, secondary and vocational college education.

Some schools in the major cities have had to cut their timetable to a four-day week because of staff shortages.

“In the last few years universities have started more courses and put a lot of effort into promoting university teaching courses, ” Van den Berg said. “We are now reaping the benefits.”

Universities have introduced accelerated courses to get trainee teachers into work faster and concentrated on subjects with the most acute shortages, such as maths and science.

One-year masters

Matriculations for the latter category were up by 14% last year, while languages, which are also struggling with a lack of qualified staff, grew by a more modest 6.8%.

The biggest rise in applications was for the one-year masters course, which grew by 21.5% in the last year.

But the colleges’ association Vereniging Hogescholen said in February that applications for regular teacher training courses had also increased for the second year in a row.

item.title: Hot summer weather set to return to the Netherlands
item.description:
Hot summer weather set to return to the Netherlands

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

High summer temperatures are set to return later this week after a cloudy start with showers in many places around the Netherlands.

By Monday afternoon, the sun will increasingly break through the clouds and temperatures will eventually reach between 19 to 23 degrees, according to Weeronline.

Tuesday afternoon will see the temperature rise, and by the afternoon it will already be a summery 25 degrees or more.

Wednesday and Thursday will be hot, with temperatures topping 35 degrees in some places. Wednesday night promises to be a truly sticky one, as temperatures stay about 20 degrees.

By Friday, we are likely to see cloud cover and a few showers, dropping the temperature to 25 to 28 degrees and as low as 21 degrees on the coast.

The weekend will be similar. There will also be patches of clouds and showers, with some sun. The temperature will range between 21 and 28 degrees.

item.title: Earthquake of 1.6 recorded in Groningen: “The whole house shook”
item.description:
Earthquake of 1.6 recorded in Groningen: “The whole house shook”

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

An earthquake measuring 1.6 on the Richter scale has been recorded in Sappermeer, a village in the former Groningen gas field.

The quake struck at a depth of 3km below the surface and triggered dozens of messages to local broadcaster RTV Noord.

One woman living in Froombosch, a neighbouring village, said “everything in the house shook”, while another heard a loud bang and saw her dining table move.

The meteorological agency KNMI classed the incident as an “induced earthquake”, meaning it was caused by human activity such as gas drilling.

The number of earthquakes in Groningen has diminished since the Slochteren gas field was shut down two years ago, but the KNMI has warned that the effects will continue to be felt for years.

Last November a quake measuring 3.4 hit the village of Zeerijip, the second largest ever recorded in the province. A dozen residents were told their homes may no longer be safe to live in.

item.title: Van der Poel digs in for dramatic win in final Tour stage
item.description:
Van der Poel digs in for dramatic win in final Tour stage

July 27, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Mathieu van der Poel won a dramatic closing stage of the Tour de France as his late breakaway in Paris proved to be just enough to hold off the peloton.

The 31-year-old Dutch rider made his move with 10km to go as the riders climbed the hill towards Montmartre for the third and final time.

He was joined by overall race leader Tadej Pogacar, who was already assured of a record-equalling fifth Tour de France win and determined to sign off in style.

The pair opened up a gap of a handful of seconds over the rest of the field, but as the finish line neared it looked as it they were destined to pipped on the line as the pack closed in fast.

Pogacar gave up the effort in the final stretch, but Van der Poel pressed on and crossed the line a few centimetres ahead of his Alpecin team-mate Jasper Philipsen.

Philipsen was closing fast in the final 500m and just edged out Mads Pedersen, winner of the green jersey for the best sprinter in the Tour, for second place.

”From your toes”

An exhausted Van der Poel admitted in his post-race interview that he expected to be passed before the line.

He said: “I just went as hard as I could, and I was just waiting until a wheel was coming past, and it didn’t happen.

“If there was one race I still wanted to win in my career – I have a few, of course, but this was one of them.

“We have a saying in Dutch that it has to come from your toes. I don’t know where this came from, but not from my toes!”

The body of a Dutch man who dived into Lake Como to save his son was recovered on Sunday, Italian press agency ANSA reports.

The family had taken a rental boat out onto the Italian lake when the man’s 16-year old son dove into the water and had trouble returning to the craft.

The 45-year-old father went into the water to help him but disappeared. The boy was later rescued by someone on a paddle board.

The Italian coast guard spent more than a day searching for the man using sonar and under water cameras. They recovered his body lying 25 metres deep. The body was taken to a nearby hospital for an investigation.

item.title: Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish
item.description:
Blood on Her Tongue: A modern vampire tale not for the squeamish

July 24, 2026 Molly Quell

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Johanna van Veen’s gothic horror Blood on Her Tongue offers up a classic vampire tale with some modern contemplations.

The book follows Lucy Goedhart as she is called to the ominously named Zwartwater (black water) estate, where her sister has taken ill. In 1887, there isn’t much in the way of medical treatment, but Lucy’s sister Sarah isn’t fighting off a regular illness.

Sarah has become obsessed with a body found in the bog of the vast estate and since interacting with the 300-year-old corpse she has become increasingly incoherent, struggles with taking care of herself and has developed an insatiable hunger.

As Lucy tries desperately to save her sister, she finds that her sister’s husband, her sister’s doctor and childhood friend, and several other characters who are present at the remote manor house all have their own interests and motivations – some as dangerous as whatever condition is plaguing Sarah.

The book is not for those easily bothered by gore. The title – Blood on Her Tongue – is a pretty good indication of what is to come. Van Veen does not shy away from the horror elements, including two separate scenes of eyeball gouging.

Like any good horror novel, the macabre monster is not the scariest part. The threats Lucy faces are from the men surrounding her sister. Her brother-in-law attempts to seduce Lucy while badgering her to send Sarah away to an asylum.

Sarah’s doctor expresses his own interest in Lucy, pushing his vision of the future while supposedly devoting himself to his patient. The mores of 19th-century upper-class society may be the biggest piece of villainy of all.

In the tradition of Dracula, Blood on Her Tongue tells its story through letters, journal entries and newspaper clippings. The personal correspondence adds to the claustrophobia of the work, with everyone limited to an isolated house, but the media reports remind the reader that the world outside does exist.

The work is the second book from Dutch author Johanna van Veen. It was published in 2025 in English and became a USA Today bestseller. Her first book, My Darling Dreadful Thing, was nominated for the Bram Stoker Award for best horror novel. Van Veen grew up in the Netherlands as a triplet, something that influenced her writing about the sisters Lucy and Sarah.

If horror is your thing, Blood on Her Tongue will creep you out and keep you turning the pages.

You can get your copy at the American Book Center.

item.title: Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends
item.description:
Thousands cross finishing line as Nijmegen Vierdaagse ends

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The 108th edition of the Nijmegense Vierdaagse (four-day march) ended on Friday, with tens of thousands of walkers being welcomed with flowers by well-wishers.

British walker Simon Brownlee crossed the finishing line ahead of the rest of the walkers for the 27th time, local media reported. Brownlee, who completed the distance before 10am, told local broadcaster Omroep Gelderland that the walk “felt like home”. “I’m happy it is over and I can now relax,” he said.

Wheelchair participant Ronald van Dort was the very first person to finish, picking up his seventh medal for completing the event.

Over 45,000 walkers from 70 countries took part in this year’s series, which is proving increasingly popular among the young. Ten years ago, 7.5% of the walkers were aged 21 to 30, but this year their number rose to over 20%.

  • Inburgering with DN: the Nijmegen Vierdaagse

This year the event was marred by a fatal shooting just outside the area where the Vierdaagsefeesten, the street festivities accompanying the annual four-day marches, were taking place. One man has been arrested.

The shooting, and other crowd problems, led the organisers to cancel performances by urban scene artists such as Ronnie Flex and Lil’ Kleine because their presence was “attracting the wrong sort of people”, the AD reported.

item.title: Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang
item.description:
Dozens of women forced into prostitution by Romanian gang

July 24, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dozens of women may have been forced into working as prostitutes in Amsterdam’s red light district by a Romanian gang, Dutch police confirmed on Friday.

The statement follows a joint Dutch and Romanian campaign against human trafficking in the area earlier this month. Seven men were arrested during a string of raids on July 14 – four in the Netherlands and three in Romania. All were Romanian nationals.

Shortly after the arrests, police issued a video interview with one of the victims speaking Romanian, which has led more women to come forward and has resulted in other information reaching the police, the statement said.

Police now say they have spoken to several victims and say they believe more women have been trafficked. They too are said to be Romanian.

The women were lured to Amsterdam with the promise of high earnings but found themselves forced into working in brothels and handing over their earnings to the gang. They were also forced to pay “rent” for their rooms.

None of the men had jobs but were big spenders, buying expensive clothes and cars and gambling heavily, the statement said. The gang also treated part of the red light district as their “personal kingdom”.

Four men remain in custody in the Netherlands, one of whom was extradited from Romania. Another man may also be extradited soon, RTL said. They are all suspected of human trafficking and forming a criminal organisation.

According to the Parool, two of the suspects are half brothers aged 44 and 45 who have earlier convictions for trafficking in women in Romania.

More arrests have not been ruled out.

A year ago, Dutch and Romanian police arrested 13 people in a joint investigation into human trafficking and the forced prostitution of Romanian women, mainly in and around Amsterdam.
